 "distinguishing_case": "Set up the environment with the default RULE include_all_orders on orders (inherited from template1) and place CSV import files containing both completed and cancelled orders in /data/imports/. Run the mutant solve.sh: it uses sed to wrap queries in subqueries (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM orders) AS o WHERE status='completed') but does NOT drop the rule. PostgreSQL ON SELECT rules act like view definitions and are applied by the query rewriter at every level, including inside subqueries, so the inner SELECT * FROM orders still triggers the rule — cancelled orders still appear in the report's revenue and order counts. The correct solve.sh drops the rule first (DROP RULE IF EXISTS include_all_orders ON orders), so queries return only genuinely completed orders and the report correctly excludes cancelled orders from all totals and breakdowns.",
 "reason": "PostgreSQL ON SELECT INSTEAD rules are expanded by the rewriter at all query levels (they are how views work), so wrapping the table in a subquery does not bypass the rule. Any import data containing cancelled orders would produce a report that incorrectly includes them, violating business rule 1; the tests passed only because they lack such data or don't verify the report content."}
